newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 6.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Prime Minister Jim Bolger staved off any immediate threat to his leadership as the National Party caucus on Tuesday decided to reaffirm his position. The decision firms Bolger's standing in coalition negotiations with NZ First, quashing speculation that National might use a change of leader as a bargaining chip to win favour with NZ First. But Bolger's medium-term future remains in doubt. Many in the party believe he lacks the ideas and energy to lead the party into the next election. Page 1.

New Zealand punters went on a betting splurge on Tuesday with the TAB enjoying a record day. Total turnover of $9,691,652 surpassed Melbourne Cup day last year when $9,439,780 was spent. Records were set on the Melbourne Cup, which attracted bets of $5,698,158, $1.4 million up on the previous record two years ago. Page 1.

Television New Zealand and Tourism Board chairman Norman Geary announced on Tuesday his retirement from both positions. Geary plans to concentrate on private-sector work. He has been in top positions in government organisations for 16 years,

including six-and-a-half years as Air New Zealand chairman. Labour Party leader Helen Clark said on Tuesday the resignation opened up the opportunity for a new government to appoint a new TVNZ chairman. Page 2.

NZ First leader Winston Peters has endorsed Prime Minister Jim Bolger's attendance at the APEC summit of leaders, isolating Labour leader Helen Clark in her complaints about New Zealand's representation. Page 2.

NZ First leader Winston Peter's appeal to the caretaker government for funds to cover coalition negotiation costs could bring in at least $100,000 for his party. Peters is refusing to answer questions on how NZ First might spend the money. Page 2.

The rising value of the New Zealand dollar against the United States dollar is a billion-dollar burden for the dairy industry, Dairy Board chairman Sir Dryden Spring says. It was the second complaint about the Kiwi's value to come from a producer board - wool industry executives complained last Thursday New Zealand's productive sector was being "skinned
alive" by the continuing rise in the currency. The Kiwi dollar had appreciated by 27 percent in the past three years against the greenback. Page 13.

Hydro lakes could be spilling water while expensive North Island themal power plants are in operation, the Major Electricity Users Group says. The group, a longtime critic of the new wholesale electricity market, made the suggestion in a report on the electricity market. The report says recent unexplained prices spikes have increased prices over many periods. Earlier this month on one day provisional prices were more than twice the forecast spot prices for 27 percent on the day. "The market is...not meeting the overall objective of ensuring lowest cost delivered energy to consumers," the group says. Page 13.

Bank of New Zealand says it will sell 45 of its branches, worth a total of $25 million, and lease them back. Customer services general manager Alan MacDonald said on Tuesday the sale was part of a strategy to ensure the bank's capital was working to develop core banking. Page 13.

TVNZ plans to bid for control of Australia's National Transmission Agency as part of a wider assault on the Australian broadcasting market, the Financial Review reported on Tuesday. TVNZ said it was in a strong position to own and operate NTA. TVNZ claimed the Australian government had "intimated to the market" that it wanted to sell NTA. Page 15.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

An Auckland health chief has delivered a stinging attack on "sloppy" public hospitals which fail to live within their budgets. South Auckland Health head Lester Levy said on Tuesday the Government should stop bailing inefficient crown health enterprises out of debt, and advocated sacking chiefs who did not perform.

Norman Geary is standing down as chairman of Television New Zealand's board but denies that he was pushed out of the job. Geary -- accused by NZ First leader Winston Peters of editorial preference in TVNZ news coverage of the Cook Islands tax affair -- is also stepping down as chairman of the Tourism Board.
NZ First on Tuesday rescued the caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger from embarrassment by publicly backing his right to attend the APEC forum this month in Manila.

People planning Australian holidays had reason to cheer and exporters cause to jeer as the value of the New Zealand dollar climbed above A90 cents for the first time since February on Tuesday. Many foreign exchange dealers think the kiwi will climb further against the Australian dollar especially if, as expected, the Reserve Bank of Australia cuts official interest rates on Wednesday.

Dublin-based Independent Newspapers has bumped its effective holding in Wilson and Horton up to 71.5 percent as Friday's expiry date for the $11 a share takeover bid nears. The offer can be extended if 48 hours' notice is given. A decision has yet to be made.

October was another bonanza month for the New Zealand sharemarket, with the NZSE gross index rising 6.5 percent in the month, prompting a 14 percent lift for the year to date, according to Craig and Co's monthly review.
Average electricity prices for some days in October will fall by up to 18 percent as a result of an interim ruling by the electricity market's surveillance committee.

The highest-ranking secured creditors of the failed Fortex Group will get nearly all their money back. Their payout was already about 96 cents to 97 cents in the dollar and would get better, said receiver Alan Isaac.
